ops.new_text: This report asks what exact-certificate architecture could eventually support primitive-geodesic ownership decisions for a source-locked Bolza surface and one frozen nonarithmetic genus-two control at \(\Lambda=21/10\). Stage 1 executed a closed-corpus literature synthesis, not a census or algorithm validation. The recorded synthesis organizes object, candidate-generation, conjugacy, root-decision, owner-semantics, rigorous-predicate, and producer-checker design questions; it does not validate their project applicability or identify a project owner. The review-adjudicated architecture permits two surface-specific exact proof producers, provided they emit one common semantic owner-certificate schema checked by an independent validator. The schema separates full-group conjugacy, maximal-root and primitivity evidence, external inversion pairing, self-reciprocity, repetitions, termination, completeness, and positive or negative replay payloads. It requires no common internal solver or input model. Production implementation remains absent. The target-empty and control-nonempty directions at the frozen cutoff are unverified inherited architecture-only assumptions. If each direction is later replayed with source- and hypothesis-adequate proof records, it may condition the corresponding producer obligation; until then neither direction is a scientific result or a basis for between-surface arithmetic inference. P33-RC-1 remains a producer-soundness, schema-interoperability, and independent-validation contract with a fail-closed not-evaluable endpoint. The contribution is a proposed interoperable certificate-methods design. A fourteen-of-fourteen match between same-lineage synthetic fixtures, their expected-outcome oracle, and their harness is retained only as a non-scientific diagnostic record, not evidence of contract correctness, independent validation, or scientific validity. This report is not a census, novelty claim, magnetic or determinant result, formal Route-A tuple, A0/A1/A2 closure, Route-A credit, or Route-B progress.

The control is the single source-locked object \texttt{NAZARENKO-EXP-OCTAGON-G2}, not a representative of all nonarithmetic surfaces. Nazarenko (2013)
% ARS-CITE use_id=P33-U06 source_ids=P33-S01 anchor=none claim_to_passage=INCONCLUSIVE locator_disposition=EXPLICIT_BOUNDED_UNAVAILABLE
\citep{P33-S01}
 and Aigon-Dupuy et al.~(2005)
% ARS-CITE use_id=P33-U07 source_ids=P33-S02 anchor=none claim_to_passage=INCONCLUSIVE locator_disposition=EXPLICIT_BOUNDED_UNAVAILABLE
\citep{P33-S02}
 remain bibliographic pointers for a future check of the construction and family setting. No retained passage establishes their relation to the exact specialization below, so these citations are not used as proof of its construction, arithmetic status, exact systole, or primitive-owner census. The frozen specialization is \(u=a=e^{-1/10}\), \(\alpha=\pi/4\), \(x=u^2=e^{-1/5}\), \(\Delta=(1-u^2)(2u^2-1)\), and \(N=-\Delta^{-1/2}\). Its proof-bearing ordered generators are
\[
 g_0=N\begin{pmatrix}u&u^2+i(1-u^2)\\u^2-i(1-u^2)&u\end{pmatrix},\quad
 g_1=N\begin{pmatrix}u&(1-u^2)+iu^2\\(1-u^2)-iu^2&u\end{pmatrix},
\]
with \(R=\operatorname{diag}(e^{i\pi/4},e^{-i\pi/4})\), \(g_2=Rg_0R^{-1}\), and \(g_3=Rg_1R^{-1}\), under the presentation
\[
 \langle g_0,g_1,g_2,g_3\mid g_0g_1^{-1}g_2g_3^{-1}g_0^{-1}g_1g_2^{-1}g_3=I\rangle .
\]
The producer input uses \(\ell(g)=2\operatorname{arcosh}(|\operatorname{tr}g|/2)\), exact admission \(\ell(g)\leq21/10\), and the finite-domain centre guard \(\lvert\alpha_g\rvert^2\leq20000\). The canonical generator-object bytes are \path{papers/28-bolza-magnetic-flow/results/round7_nonarithmetic_control_matrices.json}, SHA-256 \url{a900749b6905a5f324c2e2670363ec1bc9480481f3f5aa1240ed0ebbee55e6ca}; the bound finite certificate is \path{papers/28-bolza-magnetic-flow/results/round8_control_finite_ball_certificate.json}, SHA-256 \url{c1bf68a8a1485665680dba01d0012fb691c7ca1a795e36334639e34bbbdbcb1f}. CP must consume those exact values and digests. This is a transcription of accepted upstream locks, not a new replay, theorem, or census.

The control's nonarithmeticity is retained as an inherited-project input, not re-established here from the literature. The frozen bibliography pairs Takeuchi (1975) with a separately recorded 2006 correction
% ARS-CITE use_id=P33-U08 source_ids=P33-S03,P33-S03-CORR anchor=none claim_to_passage=INCONCLUSIVE locator_disposition=EXPLICIT_BOUNDED_UNAVAILABLE
\citep{P33-S03,P33-S03-CORR}
 and includes Popescu (2024)
% ARS-CITE use_id=P33-U09 source_ids=P33-S04 anchor=none claim_to_passage=INCONCLUSIVE locator_disposition=EXPLICIT_BOUNDED_UNAVAILABLE
\citep{P33-S04}
. The project had proposed checking an arithmetic trace-field criterion and a transcendence argument involving the inherited expression \(\exp(-1/5)\). Those are unresolved proof tasks: the retained metadata supplies neither the required source statements nor their hypotheses or a verified application to the frozen trace formula. No claim that these records supply the needed ingredients is made here. This revision neither reconstructs nor newly proves the nonarithmeticity chain, and the correction's bibliographic association does not establish its mathematical effect.

The proposed design separates candidate generation from ownership. Aurich et al.~(1991)
% ARS-CITE use_id=P33-U14 source_ids=P33-S05 anchor=none claim_to_passage=INCONCLUSIVE locator_disposition=EXPLICIT_BOUNDED_UNAVAILABLE
\citep{P33-S05}
 and Grácio and Sousa Ramos (2010)
% ARS-CITE use_id=P33-U15 source_ids=P33-S09 anchor=none claim_to_passage=INCONCLUSIVE locator_disposition=EXPLICIT_BOUNDED_UNAVAILABLE
\citep{P33-S09}
 are retained as candidates for later source review, not as verified implementations of a pathway from group data to project length-spectrum candidates. The following distinction is a project contract requirement, not a conclusion attributed to those sources: sharing a length, trace, homology class, literal word, or matrix representation does not by itself satisfy the required ownership proof. Under the frozen design, those quantities may filter or organize work, but none is accepted as a substitute for full-group conjugacy.

The proposed owner contract keeps primitive and reciprocal semantics distinct. Cherubini et al.~(2022)
% ARS-CITE use_id=P33-U16 source_ids=P33-S14 anchor=none claim_to_passage=INCONCLUSIVE locator_disposition=EXPLICIT_BOUNDED_UNAVAILABLE
\citep{P33-S14}
 and Erlandsson and Souto (2024)
% ARS-CITE use_id=P33-U17 source_ids=P33-S15 anchor=none claim_to_passage=INCONCLUSIVE locator_disposition=EXPLICIT_BOUNDED_UNAVAILABLE
\citep{P33-S15}
 remain reading pointers for a future comparison of conventions; their exact definitions, hypotheses, and relation to P33 have not been verified from retained passages. The definitions used here are the project's frozen choices, not an asserted transfer from those sources. P33 applies external inversion pairing to every oriented class, including non-self-reciprocal classes. Full conjugacy, maximal-root status, self-reciprocity, external inversion pairing, and repetition accounting therefore require independently tagged dispositions under this contract.

Domain and presentation algorithms remain proposed implementation avenues, not source-verified components of a finished cross-surface system. The bibliography includes Voight (2009)
% ARS-CITE use_id=P33-U18 source_ids=P33-S10 anchor=none claim_to_passage=INCONCLUSIVE locator_disposition=EXPLICIT_BOUNDED_UNAVAILABLE
\citep{P33-S10}
 and Despré et al.~(2023)
% ARS-CITE use_id=P33-U19 source_ids=P33-S11 anchor=none claim_to_passage=INCONCLUSIVE locator_disposition=EXPLICIT_BOUNDED_UNAVAILABLE
\citep{P33-S11}
 as candidates for checking domain construction, reduction, presentation, and termination questions. The retained records do not establish the algorithms' exact statements, input models, termination hypotheses, or applicability to either project object. Any future use must first bind those source facts and then verify the hypotheses separately for the frozen algebraic target and source-locked transcendental control. Neither a common solver nor the feasibility of either proposed pathway is inferred from the present metadata.

Epstein and Holt (2006)
% ARS-CITE use_id=P33-U20 source_ids=P33-S12 anchor=none claim_to_passage=INCONCLUSIVE locator_disposition=EXPLICIT_BOUNDED_UNAVAILABLE
\citep{P33-S12}
 and Lysenok (1990)
% ARS-CITE use_id=P33-U21 source_ids=P33-S13 anchor=none claim_to_passage=INCONCLUSIVE locator_disposition=EXPLICIT_BOUNDED_UNAVAILABLE
\citep{P33-S13}
 are retained as reading candidates for conjugacy and root-decision questions. The corrected frozen page range for the former is 287--305; a bibliographic page range is not a theorem or proof locator. Without retained source statements and hypotheses, this report does not attribute a conjugacy algorithm, positive-conjugator construction, root-extraction theorem, or project feasibility result to either record. A future implementation would still have to bind any applicable theorem, project-specific constants, canonical negative evidence, exact generator encodings, hash-stable serialization, and proof that each frozen presentation satisfies every required hypothesis.

Hoffman et al.~(2016)
% ARS-CITE use_id=P33-U25 source_ids=P33-S19 anchor=none claim_to_passage=INCONCLUSIVE locator_disposition=EXPLICIT_BOUNDED_UNAVAILABLE
\citep{P33-S19}
 and Hales et al.~(2017)
% ARS-CITE use_id=P33-U26 source_ids=P33-S20 anchor=none claim_to_passage=INCONCLUSIVE locator_disposition=EXPLICIT_BOUNDED_UNAVAILABLE
\citep{P33-S20}
 are retained as candidates for later architectural comparison, not as verified precedents supporting P33. The retained metadata does not establish their producer/checker structure, evidence objects, independence properties, or transferability to the two frozen surfaces. In the immediately following comparison paragraph, the named Hoffman and Hales comparators, the patterns attributed to them, and the stated shared features are unverified candidate-comparison hypotheses, not literature-confirmed properties of either work. The untrusted-producer and independently checkable-record requirements are P33 design proposals. No cited record validates an unbuilt P33 producer, and no proof assistant or numerical library is selected on the strength of this unverified comparison.

The notes-side trust graph is frozen at \path{notes/stage4_prime_round5_support/trust_graph.json}, SHA-256 \url{34ab38b26566ba6cc80ef1b2fdf266d7e7fe3f47af5129756ebca737611895fc}. Its proposed nodes distinguish BP, CP, their adapters, parser and predicate kernels, a fixture oracle, theorem encodings, libraries, and accountable implementers; shared schema, digest, and general-purpose-library dependencies are classified separately from disqualifying producer-decision-code reuse. The synthetic expected outcomes and provenance are recorded in \path{notes/stage4_prime_round5_support/fixture_oracle_manifest.json}, SHA-256 \url{0aadbe0af06acad88dcab573b3e3206bacef20ec237aa882568509233ae4d044}. The fixture files, expected-disposition oracle, and harness were authored by the same generator lineage. Freezing their files separately, or consuming no producer output, does not make the oracle independent of the fixtures or harness. The recorded agreement is retained solely as diagnostic provenance, not as evidence of synthetic-contract correctness, soundness, or independent validation. The component record \path{notes/stage4_prime_round5_support/component_build_provenance.json}, SHA-256 \url{56ed464ffd96fb4f8c3f604e8f94e297a1481eefd5aea52fead9f388a1fd0824}, reports zero available production components; BP, CP, both adapters, the parser, and predicate kernels remain \texttt{UNAVAILABLE\_COMPONENT\_NOT\_IMPLEMENTED}. The static exclusion audit at \path{notes/stage4_prime_round5_support/producer_code_exclusion_audit.json}, SHA-256 \url{73d6f7f9f33989a08a8ddc4123d22292e78f68d27b729f0475b2c0f9603b5a86}, is therefore \texttt{NOT\_EVALUABLE}. The trust graph records a proposed separation, not an implemented or independently verified separation. No absent source-tree, build-environment, theorem-encoding, or build hash is invented, and no validator-independence claim is made.

The notes-side fixture corpus contains exactly two files labelled valid and twelve files labelled invalid by the synthetic specification. The declared fault labels cover malformed schema, unknown proof type, altered digest, unsupported negative decision, primitive/power conflict, missing inverse link, false reciprocity, duplicate owner, unresolved cutoff, incomplete coverage, invalid termination, and hash mismatch. The existing receipt \path{notes/stage4_prime_round5_support/serialized_fixture_validation_receipt.json}, SHA-256 \url{294a80fe696be66584e13377c446cf536982bd2a9cfc1807277ad05da09c0b21}, records fourteen of fourteen outcomes matching the frozen expected dispositions and zero reported harness failures. Because one generator lineage authored the fixtures, oracle, and harness, this is only a diagnostic record of agreement with those authored expectations. It is not evidence that canonical serialization or the synthetic fail-closed contract is correct, that the declared faults provide independent coverage, or that an independent validation occurred. The subsequent fixture descriptions use \texttt{valid}, \texttt{invalid}, and \texttt{agreement} in this labelled, diagnostic sense only. These bytes are not surface records, producer outputs, owner-census results, or evidence that a production validator exists.

Package C has a notes-side synthetic diagnostic record: two files labelled canonical valid and twelve files labelled one-fault invalid have frozen expected dispositions, and the existing receipt reports fourteen of fourteen matches. The declared cases concern altered provenance digests, unrecognized proof types, unsupported negative decisions, primitive/power conflict, missing inverse links, false reciprocity, duplicate owners, unresolved cutoffs, incomplete coverage, invalid termination, malformed schema, and hash mismatch. The fixtures, oracle, and harness share one generator lineage. Their matching outcomes are retained as a record of that run, not as evidence about the synthetic contract's correctness, failure-mode coverage, or validator soundness, and not as an independent test. BP, CP, adapters, parser, production predicate kernels, and a second independently authored oracle remain unavailable. The record therefore establishes no producer-code exclusion, production-validator independence, or surface census; Package C's scientific and production obligations remain open.

The proposed interface may admit a numerical cutoff or sign witness only after its exact predicate, error justification, and applicable hypotheses have been independently established. Johansson (2017)
% ARS-CITE use_id=P33-U47 source_ids=P33-S17 anchor=none claim_to_passage=INCONCLUSIVE locator_disposition=EXPLICIT_BOUNDED_UNAVAILABLE
\citep{P33-S17}
 and Rump (2010)
% ARS-CITE use_id=P33-U48 source_ids=P33-S18 anchor=none claim_to_passage=INCONCLUSIVE locator_disposition=EXPLICIT_BOUNDED_UNAVAILABLE
\citep{P33-S18}
 remain candidates for source review, not verified support for a particular enclosure method or its use on either frozen surface. No retained passage establishes that application. Under the P33 contract, increasing numerical precision cannot substitute for the separately required nonconjugacy, maximal-root, or candidate-completeness proofs. Numerical evidence must remain subordinate to the exact group-theoretic proof type it is qualified to check; no such production predicate has been implemented here.

Fourth, production architecture remains unimplemented. Notes-side BP/CP enumeration contracts, two coverage-ledger schemas, a trust graph, a synthetic proof-registry snapshot, and a fourteen-file synthetic fixture corpus exist as design and diagnostic artifacts. The existing receipt reports fourteen of fourteen matches between same-lineage fixtures, expected outcomes, and harness decisions; this is retained as non-scientific bookkeeping, not as evidence of correct conformance, independent testing, or contract soundness. These artifacts do not supply a BP or CP producer, production adapter, parser or predicate kernel, theorem-applicability proof, independently implemented oracle, surface candidate universe, conjugacy result, root result, owner record, observed coverage digest, termination proof, or completeness certificate. Production components available remain zero, validator independence remains not evaluable, and the seven P33-RC-1 scientific/production obligations remain unimplemented.

\paragraph{AI assistance and verification limitation.}
OpenAI Codex from the GPT-5 model family assisted the recorded workflow on 2 September 2026 UTC with literature-search support, source-record and metadata checks, evidence synthesis, adversarial and role-based review, deterministic citation and hash checks, and manuscript drafting and restructuring. On 4 September 2026 UTC it also assisted with support-artifact generation, commit-pinned artifact replay, bounded identifier-endpoint replay, correction-metadata preparation, synthetic fixture and oracle preparation, BP/CP contract preparation, and deterministic support validation. The exact backend snapshot was not exposed. Liang Wang supplied the project direction and remains the accountable author; the record does not establish that he personally performed full-text or source-passage verification. The bounded replay retained no full-text body and verified no passage, so all 48 literature uses remain \texttt{anchor=none} and \texttt{claim\_to\_passage=INCONCLUSIVE}. The fixtures, expected-disposition oracle, and harness were authored in one generator lineage. Their fourteen-of-fourteen recorded agreement is retained solely as non-scientific diagnostic provenance, not as evidence of the synthetic contract's correctness or as an independent test. AI assistance, human authorization, correction metadata, and that same-lineage agreement do not establish source cleanliness, production-validator independence, theorem applicability, scientific method validity, or a surface result.
